label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
**To my friends, neighbours, the Little Acorns families, and everyone who has reached out**

Hi everyone

I’m writing one long message because my phone has not stopped since Saturday night, and I simply can’t answer everyone individually. I’m completely exhausted, but I also don’t want anyone to think their message hasn’t mattered. I’ve seen so much kindness over the past few days. I’ve cried at basically every message, sometimes properly and sometimes just sitting there with tears running down my face while trying to type “thank you”.

First, the most important thing: **I am safe. Marmalade is safe too.** We’re staying with my sister in Rondebosch, and we’re being very well looked after.

Please feel free to forward this letter to anyone who has been asking about me, including the full section about the fundraiser and the other fundraising pages going around. That part is really important.

**The short version of what happened**

The fire at Lindale Court, on Station Road in Obs, started at around 11:40pm on Saturday, 7 November. It started in a ground-floor flat, not mine. I lived on the second floor, in flat 12.

There are 14 flats in the building. Everyone got out. Two people were treated for smoke inhalation at Groote Schuur and were sent home afterwards. Given how much worse it could have been, I keep coming back to that: everyone got out.

The fire department’s current view is that it was probably caused by an electrical fault, but the investigation is still ongoing. I’m not going to speculate beyond that.

Our neighbour, Uncle Faizel, went along our floor banging on every door in his vest and slippers. That’s what woke me up. I grabbed my phone, got Marmalade, and left. Nothing else came with me. Poor Marmalade then hid under a car for two hours afterwards, which was a whole additional trauma neither of us needed.

My flat is basically gone. There is smoke and water damage everywhere, and the ceiling came down in the lounge. My landlord has said that nobody will be going back in for at least six weeks. I know there will be a lot to sort out over the coming weeks, but right now I’m taking it one day at a time. I also don’t want to keep retelling the night itself in detail, so please understand if I keep changing the subject when we speak.

Furniture can be replaced. Marmalade can’t.

**The kindness has been overwhelming**

I don’t really have the words for how people have shown up.

One of my Ladybirds’ moms left a bag of clothes at my sister’s gate at 7am on Sunday. She didn’t even knock or make me come out and talk. She just left it there where I would find it. That kind of thoughtfulness, understanding that I might need something without being ready for company, completely undid me.

There have been so many other messages, calls, offers and acts of kindness. Thank you. Please also keep the other Lindale Court residents in your thoughts. I’m not the only person whose home and belongings have been affected.

**The fundraiser, and why I’ve agreed to it**

I hate asking for help. I honestly feel very strange about having a fundraiser with my name on it. Zinhle’s response, in loving best-friend fashion, was to tell me to shut up and accept it. So I’m trying to listen to her.

Zinhle has set up a BackaBuddy page here:

**backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**

The target is **R25 000**. When I checked this morning, it was already at **R11 400**, which is honestly hard to take in. Thank you to everyone who has donated or shared it.

If sharing the fundraiser is easier for you than donating, that helps too. And please don’t feel pressured if you’re not in a position to give financially. Your messages and check-ins have already meant a great deal.

**What I actually need help with**

If anyone has been asking what would be most useful, these are the main things:

- **Help towards the deposit for a new place.** This is my biggest immediate practical worry, and it’s one of the reasons the fundraiser will make such a difference.
- **Comfortable shoes for school and some work clothes.** My shoe size is **6**, and my clothing size is **34**.
- **An old laptop, if anyone has one that still works.** Mine had all my lesson planning on it. It doesn’t need to be new or fancy; something functional that I can use for planning would be an enormous help.

Please bear with me while I work through practical arrangements and replies. I don’t want anyone putting effort into collecting something only to discover that someone else has already sorted it.

**What I don’t need right now**

Please, **no more general clothing donations for now**. People have been incredibly generous, and I already have more than I can manage. The extras I’ve received will be passed on to people in the other flats.

We also don’t need food at the moment. My sister’s freezer is full, and she is making sure I eat, even when I insist I’m not hungry.

This is not me being ungrateful. I just don’t want people spending money or time on things that are already covered.

**Please be careful: there is another “fund” going around that is not ours**

I need to be very clear about this.

A page called **“Thandi Fire Relief”** on another site is **not connected to me**. There is also a WhatsApp message asking people to make an EFT into a Capitec account. **That is not my account, and that appeal has not come from me or from Zinhle.** I have reported it.

Please don’t donate through that page, don’t EFT money to the Capitec account in that WhatsApp, and please don’t keep forwarding it as though it’s legitimate. I know people are sharing it because they want to help, which makes this especially awful.

The fundraiser I am asking people to use is the BackaBuddy link above:

**backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**

If a message or page doesn’t lead there, please check before donating or passing it on.

**For my Little Acorns families**

For those who don’t know, I teach the Ladybirds at Little Acorns Pre-Primary in Mowbray — my Grade 00 class of four- and five-year-olds.

Among the things I lost were the end-of-year concert items I had taken home to work on and laminate, including all **22 crowns** and the children’s handprint banner. That one really got me, because it wasn’t just my stuff.

But please don’t worry: **the concert on 27 November is still happening, and the Ladybirds will have crowns.** We will make a plan. Their concert is not going to disappear because of this.

I’ll be back at school on Wednesday. Please don’t make a big thing of the fire in front of the children. A normal hello and a normal school day would be the kindest thing for them and for me. I’m looking forward to seeing their little faces, and I’d like school to still feel safe and ordinary for them.

**If I don’t reply, please don’t take it personally**

I’m going to answer comments and messages slowly. I may read something, mean to reply, and then put my phone down because I’m too tired to find the words. Please don’t be offended if I don’t respond to DMs, or if my response is very short.

Thank you for checking on me, for loving me, for looking after my neighbours, and for giving me so many reminders that people can be extraordinarily good.

I’m safe. We’re safe. The rest I’ll figure out, apparently with a lot more help than I thought I was allowed to ask for.

All my love,  
**Thandi**  
(and Marmalade)
